# CI Python toolchain — ONE file, so every workflow installs identical versions.
#
# Why this file exists (card 49ab1c89): ci.yml pinned ruff/pytest/pytest-timeout/mypy while
# nightly.yml installed the same tools UNPINNED, so the nightly lane could pass or fail on a
# version no other lane used. A pin repeated in two files drifts the first time one is
# updated; a pin stated once cannot.
#
# The `==` pins are the versions this box runs (verified against .venv: ruff 0.15.20,
# pytest 9.1.1, pytest-timeout 2.4.0, mypy 2.3.1). This is the same reasoning as
# tools/install-shellcheck.sh for shellcheck: an unpinned linter drifts from the developer's
# venv and fails CI on code the local run passed (measured 2026-09-18 with ruff). A bump is a
# deliberate change: move the pin HERE, run the suite, and fix any new findings — never float it.
#
# mypy is pinned like the rest because QWEN.md requires it after any Python change; requests
# and aiohttp are installed (both ship py.typed) so mypy can RESOLVE them — the heavy optional
# deps it cannot get (torch, transformers) are declared untyped in pyproject.toml instead.
#
# Installed by .github/workflows/ci.yml (jobs: python, python-unit) and
# .github/workflows/nightly.yml (job: full-suite). Change this file once, not three times.
ruff==0.15.20
pytest==9.1.1
pytest-timeout==2.4.0
mypy==2.3.1
# pyright is pinned like the rest: it is the checker the in-repo NAS stubs (stubs/) exist
# to satisfy, and until 2026-10-09 it ran only on the developer box — a stub regression
# could not red CI.  Same reasoning as the pins above: unpinned, it drifts from the venv.
# Bump HERE and fix any new findings; never float it.
pyright==1.1.411

# Runtime deps the Python suites import. Unpinned deliberately — these were never the drift
# (only the tools above were), and pinning a scientific-stack transitive set here would be a
# second maintenance surface with no measured benefit.
pydantic
networkx
requests
aiohttp
tree-sitter
tree-sitter-bash
tree-sitter-python
